title: gpu-pool-autoscaler-config-entropy-debug-scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
This scratchpad captures the debugging thread for the recent afternoon GPU pool throughput collapses (week of 2024-11-04). The signal looked like sudden effective capacity drops in specific dedicated pools, followed by noisy tenant exacerbation and repeated autoscale churn. This doc is intentionally messy — log snips, ad-hoc commands, short hypotheses, and quick mitigations we tried.

Top-level hypothesis (working):
- Root cause is a configuration interaction between the cluster autoscaler backoff parameters, the pool-level eviction thresholds, and a KV-cache amplification pattern from a handful of long-context chat sessions. When autoscaler triggers partial instance termination and quick re-adds, tenant assignment + soft-affinity causes temporary oversubscription on a subset of hosts (noisy neighbor). Amplification then looks like a pool-level degradation.

Timeline (abridged):
- 2024-11-04 15:37 UTC: First latency spike alert (p95 token latency increase) for pool:dedicated-eu-west-3
- 15:40 UTC: SRE oncall (Omar) notes 25% increase in eviction events; allocator logs show repeated scale-down then scale-up within 5m windows
- 15:45 UTC: Engineers observe 3 hosts with >85% GPU utilisation while pool reported only 60% average — sign of uneven tenant packing
- 16:10 UTC: Temporary mitigations applied (see below); visible latency improvement at 16:32 UTC

Observations and logs (snips):
- allocator logs: "scale_event: type=down reason=low_util backoff_ms=60000 instance_group=dedicated-eu-west-3 pool=chat-large vms_terminated=2"
- scheduler trace: "packing_decision tenant=customer-42 preferred_host=h-07 affinity_score=0.82 forced_reassign=true"
- kv-cache metrics: tenant=customer-42 kv_cache_hit_rate=0.03 kv_cache_size=1.9GB active_sessions=14
- host telemetry: h-07 gpu_mem_used=15.1GB gpu_util=90% processes=[kclient:3, runtime:5]

Quick mitigations attempted (what we did, why, result):
1) Increase autoscaler stable window from 60s -> 180s (temp)
   - Rationale: reduce oscillation where scale-down immediately followed by scale-up
   - Command: kubectl patch hpa/ai-inference-autoscaler -n infra --patch 'spec: {behavior: {scaleDown: {stabilizationWindowSeconds: 180}}}'
   - Result: fewer immediate re-adds; pool-level oscillation reduced but not eliminated

2) Bump eviction threshold for soft-affinity tenants by +5% on the pool
   - Rationale: stop premature eviction of long-context sessions causing cache warmup/rehits
   - Mechanism: set pool config param eviction_soft_threshold=0.65 -> 0.7
   - Result: cache warming improved for customer-42 but overall host imbalance persisted

3) Manual tenant rebalancing (rough): drain-heavy-host h-07 and spread tenants across three underutilized hosts
   - Commands: deallocate_tenant --host h-07 --tenants "customer-42,customer-99"; scheduler rebalance
   - Result: immediate relief on h-07; but this was manual and temporary

What we measured after mitigations:
- p95 latency dropped from 420ms -> 210ms over 20m
- pool average util remained ~63% but standard deviation across hosts dropped from 22% -> 9%
- KV-cache miss rate for customer-42 reduced to 0.12 from 0.55 after session spreading

Open hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Autoscaler backoff/stabilization settings allow partial scale-down while eviction thresholds are too aggressive; combined, they create repeated reassignments that cause hot-spotting. (most likely)
- H2: Scheduler affinity scoring is too deterministic for recent placement changes; it over-concentrates similar sessions on hosts with warm caches to favour locality — but when autoscaler terminates an instance, warm cache gets lost and sessions pile onto remaining warm hosts. (likely)
- H3: A subtle bug in the allocator's scoring when host GPU memory crosses 14GB boundary; observed host telemetry shows process count increase that correlates with eviction churn. (possible)

Repro experiment plan (short):
- Synthetic load generator: spin multiple long-context sessions that produce KV-cache amounts similar to customer-42; ramp up on a test dedicated pool with autoscaler set to production values and then toggle stabilization windows.
- Metrics to collect: per-host gpu_util, kv_cache_size, tenant_placement_entropy (new metric), autoscale_events, scheduler_decision_trace
- Expected signal if H1 true: lowering stabilization window in test leads to more autoscale events and host placement entropy drops prior to degradation

Temporary follow-ups (next 72h):
- Keep autoscaler stable window at 180s for pools with high long-context churn (prod config change ticket: JIRA-ENG-8551)
- Add quick guard: if host GPU util > 85% and pool host_stddev > 20% then pause further scale-downs for 5m (hook for allocator) — experiment in staging first (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/378)
- Add a scheduler probe that computes tenant_placement_entropy hourly; alert if entropy < 0.5 for >15m

Longer-term actions:
- Rework scheduler affinity scoring to include an entropy regularizer (reduce deterministic packing) — design doc needed (owner: Priya)
- Revisit eviction thresholds per workload-class (chat-longcontext vs short-generation)
- Instrument allocator to emit more granular placement decisions (trace ids) for postmortem correlation with autoscale events

Notes to self / oncall cheat sheet (quick):
- When you see p95 spike + repeated scale events: first check autoscaler events (metric autoscaler.events.rate) and host_std_dev util metric; if stddev > 18% prioritize pausing scale-downs
- To apply quick stabilization: kubectl patch hpa ... stabilizationWindowSeconds=180 (undo later)
- To revert eviction bump: edit pool config in infra-config repo under pools/dedicated-*/eviction.yaml

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Need to determine whether the autoscaler backoff should be machine-group granular or pool-granular. Current change was pool-granular; there may be cross-pool interference.
- Validate whether KV-cache persistence across instance terminations is properly attempted; there may be a race when reassigning sessions where cache repopulation causes burst IO and process spawning.
- Add a synthetic test into our CI that simulates autoscaler churn + long-context workloads and fails if placement entropy collapses

Appendix: useful queries and commands (oncall friendly)
- kubectl get hpa -n infra ai-inference-autoscaler -o yaml | grep stabilizationWindowSeconds -A2
- allocator logs: gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.cluster_name="dedicated-eu-west-3" AND jsonPayload.component="allocator"' --limit 200 --order=desc
- placement entropy snapshot: psql -c "select host, count(distinct tenant_id)/count(*) as entropy from placements where ts > now()- interval '15 minutes' group by host;"

End of scratchpad. Keep this doc as the running capture of debugging decisions; once we triage fully we'll produce a cleaner postmortem and a prioritized action list.
